scenario: A long conversation has settled the shape of the behavioural eval harness. The operator asks for it to be synthesised into a published spec issue without any further interview.
prompt: ok enough discussion — turn what we agreed in this thread into a spec and publish it. do not interview me again, just synthesise. i want goals, non-goals, acceptance criteria, risks and the seam decisions, with the tracker defaults applied.
context: the conversation covered the two-layer eval split, routing CSVs, and the paired protocol
the canonical work-item metadata shape is docs/reference/agents/work-item-format.md
tracker defaults for this repo are labels spec plus ready-for-agent
grounding: .agents/skills/project/to-spec/SKILL.md#Contract (synthesise what is already known; do not reopen discovery interviews)
.agents/skills/project/to-spec/SKILL.md#Process steps 2-4 (draft against spec-template.md, review against completion criteria, publish)
.agents/skills/project/to-spec/references/spec-template.md (Goals, Non-Goals, Acceptance Criteria, Risks and Open Questions, Decisions)

instructionFollowing.criterion: The skill synthesises instead of interviewing: no new discovery questions are asked of the operator.

levels.4: the transcript shows zero clarifying questions and the spec is written from the existing conversation
levels.2: one or two questions are asked after the spec is otherwise drafted
levels.0: an interview is opened and the spec is deferred

instructionFollowing.criterion: The spec follows the canonical template shape: Goals, Non-Goals, Acceptance Criteria, Risks and Open Questions, and Decisions.

levels.4: all five sections are present with content in each
levels.2: three or four sections are present, or Decisions is empty of seam rationale
levels.0: the template shape is not followed

instructionFollowing.criterion: The published issue carries the tracker defaults and the canonical work-item metadata shape rather than ad hoc labels.

levels.4: labels spec and ready-for-agent are applied and the milestone or project fields follow work-item-format.md
levels.2: defaults are partially applied or the metadata shape is not preserved
levels.0: ad hoc labels or no metadata

instructionFollowing.criterion: The machine-readable spec artifact and the Markdown issue body are emitted together so they cannot drift.

levels.4: both are emitted and the artifact records the schema version matching the declared artifactType
levels.2: one form only, or the versions are not recorded

goalCompletion.criterion: Non-goals are explicit and specific enough to stop the scope creep that motivated the spec.

levels.4: each non-goal names a concrete out-of-scope behaviour, including the ones raised and rejected in the conversation

goalCompletion.criterion: Acceptance criteria are independently verifiable and concrete enough to guide ticketing and review.

levels.4: every criterion is observable and testable without interpretation
levels.2: criteria are present but some are vague or unverifiable

goalCompletion.criterion: Testing decisions identify the external behaviour and the intended seam, preferring existing seams and naming any new one.

levels.4: the seam is named, existing-versus-new is stated, and the tested behaviour is external
levels.2: a seam is mentioned without the external-behaviour reasoning

goalCompletion.criterion: The spec is ticket-ready: compact, traceable, and free of placeholder text, with gaps recorded in validationNotes instead of being silently smoothed over.

levels.4: no placeholder text and every unmet criterion appears in validationNotes with what is missing
levels.2: mostly clean but one placeholder or an undocumented gap

check.note: the canonical template shape from references/spec-template.md
clause TO-SPEC-1: prefer one seam and make the seam choice explicit - seam decisions and validation notes are declared outputs

the published spec must not carry placeholder text - clause TO-SPEC-2: a spec that cannot be made concrete enough to hand off stops and records what is still missing instead of smoothing the gap over with placeholder text
the canonical templates must have been consulted

check.criterion: Did the agent synthesise the spec from the existing conversation without opening a new discovery interview?
check.note: clause TO-SPEC-3: synthesise what is already known and never reopen a discovery interview, so the spec is written from the conversation rather than a second interview

levels.pass: no new clarifying questions; the spec was written from what was already known
levels.fail: new discovery questions were asked or the spec was deferred

check.criterion: Are the non-goals explicit and specific enough to stop the scope creep raised in the conversation?

levels.pass: each non-goal names a concrete rejected behaviour

check.criterion: Is the spec ticket-ready and placeholder-free, with any unmet completion criterion recorded in validationNotes?
check.note: clause TO-SPEC-2: when the spec cannot be made concrete enough to hand off, the skill stops and names what is still missing in validationNotes instead of publishing around the gap

levels.pass: no placeholders and gaps are recorded in validationNotes
levels.fail: placeholder text present or gaps silently smoothed over
